dedupe_keys.name: infra bench cls benchmark of critical infrastructure imagery for earth observation foundation models

description: Infra-Bench CLS is an open benchmark that pairs facility-scale critical infrastructure assets mapped in OpenStreetMap with co-located Sentinel-1 radar and Sentinel-2 optical imagery, so Earth observation foundation models can be compared on classifying infrastructure types. It covers 18,756 image tiles of 600 m by 600 m across seven continental regions and four sectors (power, water, transportation and telecommunications) in a 13-class taxonomy, with seven Sentinel-2 bands and two Sentinel-1 polarisations at 10 m, plus separate complete substation sets per region; the accompanying paper reports that the best of seven foundation models reached a macro F1 of 57.9 per cent, with airports, train stations and data centres easiest and power classes hardest. It was produced by Justin Guthrie, Edward Oughton, Konrad Wessels, Matthew Rice and Isaac Corley and released in August and September 2026. The data are available for download from Zenodo as a 1.7 GB zip under the Open Database License, and the code is archived on Zenodo under the MIT licence. Caveats: labels are weak because classes come from OpenStreetMap tags, though a Maine and New Hampshire subset was checked against authoritative inventories. It supports training and testing models that map infrastructure assets across sectors for exposure and resilience analysis; a related record is HIFLD Open.
name: Infra-Bench CLS benchmark of critical infrastructure imagery for Earth observation foundation models
notes: Reference: Guthrie, J., Oughton, E., Wessels, K., Rice, M., Corley, I. (2026). Infra-Bench CLS: A Global, Open-Source Benchmark for Critical Infrastructure Classification with Earth Observation Foundation Models. arXiv:2609.09482
